Gold exploration and development company working the historic Homestake district of the Black Hills, South Dakota, one of the richest gold camps in US history. Main assets are the Homestake District Consolidation project (Richmond Hill deposit, with a pre-feasibility study) and nearby Maitland and Blind Gold prospects. Created in 2022 when Dakota Territory Resource Corp combined with a SPAC; listed on NYSE American (DC). It has no producing mine and no revenue, funding itself through equity raises. B2B resource company with almost no consumer brand awareness.

Community bank, the banking subsidiary of Enterprise Bancorp (Nasdaq: EBTC). Offers commercial lending, cash management, retail checking and savings, mortgages and wealth management to small and mid-sized businesses, professionals, nonprofits and households across northeastern Massachusetts and southern New Hampshire, with roughly 25 branches and around $4.5bn in assets. Founded in 1988. Independent Bank Corp (Rockland Trust) agreed to acquire it in 2024 and completed the deal in March 2025, so it no longer operates as a separate bank. Regional brand with local sponsorship activity only.

Small US oil and gas producer, formerly the SPAC HNR Acquisition Corp, which completed a business combination with Pogo Resources in 2023 and relisted on NYSE American as EON Resources (EONR). Revenue comes from selling crude oil and natural gas from mature onshore fields operated mainly in Texas and Oklahoma, with a strategy of buying and optimising legacy producing assets. Very small by industry standards, thinly traded and highly indebted. B2B commodity seller with no consumer brand profile and little marketing budget.

Canadian gold exploration company spun out of the Auryn Resources / Eskay Mining reorganisation in 2020. Holds three projects: Eau Claire in the James Bay region of Quebec, the Committee Bay belt in Nunavut, and Last Chance in Quebec. Funded through equity raises rather than operations, with no production or product revenue; has backing from large mining investors. Listed on the TSX and NYSE American under FURY. Pure exploration play serving the gold market, with no consumer visibility.

Closed-end investment fund managed by Gabelli Funds, part of the GAMCO Investors / Gabelli family of vehicles led by Mario Gabelli. It invests mainly in shares of media, telecommunications and related content companies and pays regular distributions to shareholders. Trades on the NYSE under GGT; income comes from dividends and capital gains on its portfolio, and the manager earns a management fee. Sold to retail and income-seeking investors through brokers. A financial vehicle with essentially no operating business, so no consumer brand and no sponsorship rationale.

Calgary-based junior oil and gas producer listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (GXE). Produces light and heavy crude oil plus natural gas from conventional properties in Alberta and Saskatchewan, including Hamilton Lake, Swan Hills and Oungre areas, at roughly 10,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Sells output to midstream buyers at market prices, so revenue tracks oil prices and hedging. Small-cap, B2B commodity producer with minimal public brand recognition.

Israeli clean-energy hardware maker developing alkaline fuel cells that generate backup and off-grid power from hydrogen and, in its newer products, from ammonia (GenCell G5, G5rx and the GenCell A5 ammonia-to-power unit). Targets telecom towers, utilities, data centres and critical infrastructure needing reliable backup in place of diesel generators; sells units plus service contracts. Founded in 2011 and listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange in 2021. B2B equipment supplier with little consumer recognition.

Exploration and development company focused on high-purity manganese for battery materials. Its K.Hill project in southeastern Botswana is being developed to produce high-purity manganese sulphate monohydrate, a precursor for lithium-ion battery cathodes used in electric vehicles. Planned customers are battery and cathode makers in Europe and Asia. Pre-revenue, funded by equity and listed on the TSX Venture Exchange with a secondary listing in Frankfurt. B2B critical-minerals developer, no consumer brand.

Guernsey-registered, London-listed specialist finance group that invested in alternative small-business lenders, including peer-to-peer and invoice-finance businesses such as Funding Path, Sancus and Fintech Alts. Revenue came from interest and fees on loans to small and medium UK companies and from realisations of its holdings. After a restructuring around 2018 it was renamed Sancus Lending Group. Few retail consumers have heard of it; its business is B2B lending, so brand visibility is low.

Silver exploration company advancing the Plomosas silver project in Sinaloa, Mexico, which includes the San Marcial mine area, a historic silver-zinc-lead district it consolidated and is drilling to define resources. The company is pre-revenue and relies on equity financing; its outcome depends on drilling results and silver prices. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under GRSL. B2B junior miner with no consumer brand or marketing profile.

Silver and gold producer with operations in Mexico, headquartered in Vancouver. Holds mines and mills in the Guanajuato state, including the Valenciana mine complex and the Cata mine, plus the Topia silver-lead-zinc mine in Durango acquired in 2023. Sells concentrates to smelters and traders; output is modest and the company has carried debt while ramping up. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (GSVR). B2B miner with no consumer brand.

Developer of low-latency video streaming and contribution technology. Products include Makito X encoders and decoders, the Haivision Hub and StreamHub video platforms, Kraken video wall hardware, and the open-source SRT protocol it helped create. Customers are broadcasters, sports producers, government and defence agencies, corporates and healthcare/education; revenue mixes hardware, software and subscriptions, roughly US$120m a year. Listed on the TSX (HAI), with R&D and sales in North America and Europe. B2B vendor, known inside the broadcast industry but not to consumers.

Exploration-stage mining company focused on silver and other precious metals, based in Toronto. Operates as a junior explorer funded by equity raises on the Canadian market. No production, products or consumer business could be confirmed from the information available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Maker of portable oxygen concentrators for people with chronic lung conditions such as COPD, led by the Inogen One G5 and the smaller Rove 6. Patients get a lightweight battery-powered device they carry around instead of heavy oxygen tanks. Sells mostly direct to consumers through its call-centre sales model and to home medical equipment dealers, with Medicare and insurance reimbursement important to demand and rental income; annual revenue in the $300m+ range. Listed on Nasdaq (INGN). Recognised among oxygen patients and clinicians, little general public awareness.

Small US holding company that owns niche operating businesses, listed over-the-counter as JANL. The largest unit is Janel Group, a freight forwarder and customs broker moving cargo by air and sea for importers and exporters. Others include Indco, a maker of industrial mixers, and a life sciences group (Antibodies Inc., Aves Labs and related reagent suppliers). Revenue approaches $200m, majority from logistics. B2B, with little public brand awareness.

Lithium exploration and development company with its core Itinga project in the Minas Gerais lithium district of Brazil, including the Bandeira deposit, aiming at spodumene concentrate for battery makers. Pre-revenue, funded through equity and strategic investors, and listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (LTH). Competes with other Brazilian lithium juniors; if built, customers would be cathode makers and traders. B2B resource developer without consumer brand awareness.

Canadian-listed junior resource company based in Toronto. The data points to mining exploration or manufacturing-related activity but gives no project, product or financial detail. Its identity cannot be confirmed reliably from the information available, so no further claims are made. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Nordic streaming and media group, spun out of Modern Times Group in 2018 and renamed Viaplay Group in 2022. Runs the Viaplay streaming service, Viaplay-branded sports and entertainment TV channels, a film and series studio business, and commercial radio in the Nordics and Baltics. It held Formula 1 rights in the Nordics and the Netherlands before pulling back from many markets after losses and a financial restructuring in 2023-24. Revenue came from subscriptions and advertising, in the billions of Swedish kronor. Well-known consumer streaming brand in Scandinavia.

Gold and antimony explorer listed on both the Australian Securities Exchange and Nasdaq (NVA). Its flagship is the Estelle Gold Project in the Tintina Gold Belt of Alaska, with a large resource across the RPM, Korbel and Train zones, plus antimony discovery at the Stibium prospect that has attracted US government and defence-supply interest. Pre-revenue and equity funded. B2B explorer with little consumer awareness.

Community bank and subsidiary of Old Second Bancorp (Nasdaq: OSBC). Provides commercial real estate and business lending, treasury services, mortgages and consumer deposits to businesses and households around Chicago's western and southern suburbs, with about 50 branches and around $6bn in assets. Founded in 1871. Local retail bank known in its metro market but not nationally. The bank is among the larger community banks in the Chicago suburbs and offers online and mobile banking as well as branches.

The Philippines' largest telecoms and digital services company, listed in Manila (TEL) and on the NYSE (PHI). Operates fixed line, fibre broadband (PLDT Home), mobile networks through Smart Communications and Sun Cellular, plus enterprise ICT, data centres and digital payments via Maya. Serves tens of millions of consumer mobile subscribers and the country's businesses. Part of the MVP Group led by Manuel V. Pangilinan, with NTT and KKR as notable investors. A household name in the Philippines with a long record of sports sponsorship.

US consumer wellness company, formerly Jupiter Wellness, behind Safety Shot, a drink it markets as helping lower blood alcohol content after drinking. Product sold in retail and online as a ready-to-drink beverage and in sachet or powder form, aimed at adult social drinkers and the on-premise trade. Small, loss-making company listed on Nasdaq (SHOT), with total sales still modest. Consumer product with limited but growing shelf distribution.

Copper development business linked to ASX-listed miner Sandfire Resources, which operates the Motheo mine in Botswana and the MATSA complex in Spain. The North American arm holds the Black Butte copper project in Montana, which came with Sandfire's acquisition of Tintina Resources. The project seeks permitting and financing rather than producing copper. Corporate parent is a mid-tier miner with several thousand staff worldwide; the subsidiary itself has no consumer brand.

Cybersecurity company offering managed detection and response and extended detection services through its Taegis XDR platform, plus incident response and threat intelligence. Customers are mid-sized and large enterprises and public bodies worldwide; revenue is mostly subscriptions, around $350m a year before acquisition. Founded in 1999 and spun out of Dell, which held the majority stake. Listed on Nasdaq (SCWX) until Sophos bought it in a deal announced in late 2024 and completed in early 2025. B2B brand known to security buyers only.

Chinese company based in Jinan, Shandong, whose activity spans energy, oil and gas and plastics according to its Crunchbase tags. It appears to be a listed domestic business in the Shengli oilfield region, but its products, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed from the information available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Creative platform that connects brands and artists, running crowdsourced design and creative challenges for companies such as Coca-Cola, Dell and Volvo, plus talent-management and licensing services built around a network of millions of creators. Co-founded in 2007 and promoted by celebrities including Ashton Kutcher. Revenue from brand-commissioned creative contests and creative-services fees. It later pursued a listing and blockchain-related ventures. Known mainly among marketing agencies and creative communities.

Gold-copper exploration company advancing the Treaty Creek project in the Golden Triangle of northwestern British Columbia, near Seabridge's Kerr-Sulphurets-Mitchell and Newmont's Brucejack. Holds the Goldstorm and Copper Belle zones, with a resource estimate expanded by ongoing drilling. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (TUD) and funded by equity raises, with no operating revenue. B2B junior explorer without consumer visibility. The company holds a majority interest in the claims, with a partner holding the remainder, and its drill results are closely watched by Golden Triangle investors.

Gold exploration company holding a large land package in Yukon's White Gold district near Dawson City, a district known for the Coffee gold discovery and other placer-and-lode finds. Work consists of soil sampling, trenching and drilling to define new targets, financed through equity and joint ventures. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under WGO. Early-stage and pre-revenue, with no consumer brand profile.

Australian lithium developer listed on the ASX (WR1), advancing the Cancet and Adina spodumene projects in the James Bay region of Quebec, Canada. It has been working towards resource upgrades and an off-take and funding strategy with investors, aiming to supply lithium concentrate to battery supply chains in North America and Asia. Pre-revenue and equity funded. Has had regional strategic investors. B2B explorer, not known to consumers.

Malaysian consumer finance company, a subsidiary of Japan's AEON Financial Service. Offers AEON credit cards, personal financing, easy-payment instalment plans for goods bought at retailers and car dealers, and motorcycle and vehicle financing, with a large customer base across Malaysia and a network of branches and merchants. Listed on Bursa Malaysia (AEONCR). Retail brand recognised by Malaysian consumers, often through links to AEON malls and retail group.

Romania's leading aluminium producer and the largest integrated aluminium complex in Central and Eastern Europe, with an alumina refinery link, a primary smelter, and casthouses producing ingots, billets, slabs and wire rod. Customers are European manufacturers in automotive, construction and packaging. It also owns Alprom, a rolling mill, and Alro is majority controlled by Cyprus-based Vimetco. Listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (ALR); revenue runs to around RON 3-4bn. Heavy-industry B2B brand, known locally but not by consumers.

Silver exploration and development company with two flagship assets: Cerro Las Minitas, a silver-zinc-lead project in Durango, Mexico, and the historic Calico silver project in California's Mojave Desert, plus other US holdings. Business is drilling and resource expansion funded by equity, with potential sale or partnering later. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (APGO). Pre-revenue B2B explorer with no consumer brand.

Nevada-based metals recycler built around AquaRefining, an electrochemical process to recover lead from used batteries, and now pivoted towards recycling lithium-ion battery materials with a hydrometallurgical approach. Operates a plant in the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center; customers are battery makers, smelters and metals traders. Founded in 2014 and listed on Nasdaq (AQMS). Revenue is minimal and losses persist, but the story appeals to EV and sustainability investors.

Gold exploration company listed on the ASX (AUC), centred on the Katanning gold project in Western Australia's Great Southern region, where it has defined a multi-million-ounce resource and is progressing towards a development decision. Also holds the Dumbleyung project. Funding comes from equity raises and strategic investors, with no production revenue. B2B explorer with limited brand visibility outside investor circles.

Online lead-generation and marketing business for the car industry, formerly Autobytel, which renamed itself AutoWeb in 2017. Runs consumer car-research sites including Autobytel.com, AutoUSA and Car.com, and sells purchase-intent leads and advertising to dealers and automakers. Revenue declined as buyer behaviour shifted to bigger platforms. Listed on Nasdaq (AUTO) until it moved to a smaller venue. Brand is known to dealers, and to some consumers via its sites.

Chinese tea brand and retailer, widely known as Bama Tea (Ba Ma), selling Anxi Tieguanyin oolong, Wuyi rock tea, Pu'er, white and black teas through a large chain of mostly franchised stores plus e-commerce. Positions itself as a premium traditional-tea retailer with gift packaging, serving consumers and corporate gifting buyers. Shows several thousand points of sale and seeks a Hong Kong stock exchange listing. Recognised retail brand in China, low profile abroad.

Australian graphite developer listed on the ASX (BKT), with its principal asset the Mahenge Liandu project in Tanzania, designed to supply flake graphite to battery anode makers and industrial users. It pursued a feasibility study and off-take talks while the Tanzanian government held a free-carried interest. Pre-revenue and equity funded. B2B resource company with no consumer brand. Its development plan depends on project financing, off-take agreements with anode makers and Tanzanian permits, and revenue only starts once a mine is built.

Quebec gold explorer working along the Cadillac-Larder Lake fault zone near Val-d'Or, with the Chimo mine property, the Benoist and Fayolle projects and other holdings, some in partnership with larger producers. Spends on drilling and resource definition and pays for it through equity placements. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (ECR). Pre-revenue explorer without consumer brand presence. It has also relied on option agreements and partner funding to advance neighbouring Abitibi properties known for historic gold production.

US consumer and specialty products maker behind Arm & Hammer baking soda, laundry detergent and cat litter, OxiClean, Trojan condoms, First Response pregnancy tests, Waterpik, Batiste dry shampoo, Spinbrush, Zicam, Vitafusion gummies and Hero acne patches, plus a specialty products unit. Sells mainly through mass retailers and online, with annual revenue around $6bn. Founded in 1846 and listed on the NYSE (CHD). Household brands in North America with growing international sales; sponsorship has historically been through individual brands.

Mineral developer whose principal asset is the Cinovec lithium and tin project in the Czech Republic, held through a joint venture with CEZ Group to build a mine and processing plant supplying battery-grade lithium chemicals to European gigafactories. Listed on the ASX and London's AIM (EMH). Pre-revenue; progress depends on European battery supply-chain policy and permitting. B2B developer with no consumer brand.

Montreal-based company whose Crunchbase tags point to energy, finance and mining, suggesting a royalty or resource-investment vehicle for strategic elements. No products, projects or financial detail can be confirmed from the information available. The source entry offers no usable company description, so products, customers and size remain unverified. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Chinese information-technology company with activities linked to aerospace and mobile enterprise software, apparently providing software and systems services to large organisations. The headquarters listed and the specific products and customers cannot be confirmed from the information available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Canadian nickel developer advancing the Baptiste nickel project in central British Columbia, a large low-grade deposit of awaruite, a natural nickel-iron alloy that can be recovered without conventional smelting and produce low-carbon nickel for stainless steel and EV batteries. Backed by Baiyin, a Chinese state mining group, as strategic investor. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (FPX). Pre-revenue B2B developer with no consumer brand.

Critical-minerals company in Quebec with two angles: the Montviel rare-earth deposit in the northern part of the province, and a patented rare-earth and magnet-recycling process developed through its Innovation Metals subsidiary, aimed at producing neodymium and praseodymium oxides without radioactive waste. Customers would be magnet and electronics manufacturers. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (GMA). Pre-revenue; no consumer brand. Its approach is to supply rare-earth oxides for permanent magnets used in electric vehicles and wind turbines from a cleaner, domestic source in Canada.

Gold exploration company whose main project is Elk Gold in south-central British Columbia, near Merritt. Plans to restart and grow a small-scale open-pit operation from past production, with permits and resource work under way. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (GMTN). Pre-revenue and equity funded; B2B resource company with no consumer visibility. Past work on the property includes earlier drilling and a small historical operation, and it is a small, thinly capitalised company in the British Columbia interior.

Gold-copper explorer with a focus on the Dominican Republic, where it controls the Romero copper-gold project in the San Juan Province, near Barrick's Pueblo Viejo mine. Drilling and resource estimates are the main activity, funded by equity raises and partners. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (GQC). Pre-revenue B2B explorer without consumer visibility. The Dominican Republic has a long mining history and is a growing destination for gold-copper exploration, which supports the company's investment case.

Fabless semiconductor company that designs high-performance static RAM (SRAM) memory chips for networking, telecom, military and aerospace customers, and is building an in-memory associative processing unit (APU, Gemini-I) for AI search and edge workloads. Revenue is under $30m a year, from customers such as Nokia and defence primes. Founded in 1995 and listed on Nasdaq (GSIT). B2B component supplier, known to engineers rather than consumers.

Bank holding company for Heartland Bank and Trust, a community bank with about 60 branches in central and northern Illinois, serving small businesses, farmers, real estate investors and households with loans, deposits, treasury and wealth services. Roughly $5bn in assets and a long record of dividend payments. Listed on Nasdaq (HBT) since a 2019 IPO. Regional brand with strong local presence.

Israeli maker of digital finishing machines for packaging and printing, notably the Highcon Beam and Euclid platforms that cut and crease folding cartons and corrugated board using lasers and digital tools rather than physical dies. Customers are packaging converters, printers and brand owners wanting short runs and quick turnaround. Backed by venture and strategic investors including Hewlett-Packard Israel and the company has sold hundreds of machines globally. B2B supplier with little public brand awareness.

Geospatial company providing three-dimensional digital elevation and terrain data, produced from airborne radar (IFSAR) surveys and sold as NEXTMap data, plus analytics. Customers include governments, defence, insurers, utilities, aviation, mapping and infrastructure planners. Roughly $20m in annual revenue. Operates from Denver with an international footprint. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (IMP). B2B data vendor, not visible to the public.

Offshore and onshore engineering, procurement and construction contractor serving oil, gas and renewable energy clients: builds and refurbishes jack-up drilling rigs, constructs offshore platforms, and delivers wind and gas industry projects. Operates yards in the UAE (Hamriyah, Sharjah) and Saudi Arabia. It was previously on the London Stock Exchange and delisted in 2021, after financial pressure and a refinancing. Customers are national oil companies and rig owners. B2B contractor with a low profile outside the energy industry.

Gold producer with the San Albino mine in Nicaragua's Nueva Segovia department, which it brought into production after acquiring it from the Nicaraguan owners and shifting from small-scale mining to mechanised operations. Gold sold to international refiners. Also holds exploration claims elsewhere in Central America. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (MKO). Small, B2B, with little brand awareness beyond investors.

Surgical robotics company, spun out of MicroPort Scientific in 2021 and listed in Hong Kong (2252). Develops the Toumai laparoscopic surgical robot, orthopedic robot and endovascular and percutaneous systems, selling to hospitals in China and abroad as part of a global drive. Revenue comes from system sales, instruments and service. One of China's largest surgical robot developers, competing with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci. Brand known among hospitals and clinicians.

Australian company running a metals recovery and critical-minerals strategy: through its US subsidiary Flash Metals, it works with Flash Joule Heating technology licensed from Rice University to extract gallium, germanium, rare earths and precious metals from mining and electronic waste. It also holds early-stage mineral exploration interests alongside its recycling work. Listed on the ASX (MTM). Early-stage and funded by equity raises, with no revenue to speak of and no consumer exposure.

Silver and strategic minerals company developing the Silver Sand project in Bolivia, a large high-grade silver deposit in the Potosi department, and holding the Carangas silver project, also in Bolivia. Formed in 2019 as a spin-off from Silvercorp Metals, which remains a major shareholder. Pre-revenue; aims to build a mine and sell concentrates. Listed on the NYSE American and TSX (NEWP, NUAG). B2B miner with no consumer brand.

Silver and gold exploration company whose flagship is the Santa Ana silver project in Colombia's Tolima department, a historic high-grade district near Colombia's Ibague. Work focuses on drilling and permitting, funded by equity raises and strategic investors. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (OCG). Pre-revenue B2B explorer, little consumer awareness. The company promotes high-grade silver intercepts to attract investors and works with local communities and Colombian authorities on exploration permits.

Australian polymetallic miner that restarted the Endeavor zinc-lead-silver mine near Cobar in New South Wales, one of the country's largest silver-lead-zinc deposits, and also holds the Hera gold-base metals project. Sells concentrates to smelters and traders. Listed on the ASX (POL) after a restructure and funding from investors. B2B producer, with limited public recognition. The mine sits in the Cobar mineral field, which hosts a number of copper and gold operations, and Polymetals aims to expand output through further drilling.

Pennsylvania community bank, subsidiary of Riverview Financial Corporation, with a network of branches in central Pennsylvania offering business and consumer lending, deposits and wealth management for local families and companies. Riverview was listed on Nasdaq (RIVE) and merged into Mid Penn Bancorp in 2021, ending separate operation. Regional retail brand without national reach. The bank serves farms, local businesses and professionals, and its lending is concentrated in commercial real estate and small business credit.

Australian mineral explorer listed on the ASX (RTR) with the Earaheedy zinc-lead-silver project in Western Australia's Earaheedy Basin, a major discovery where it holds a joint venture with Zenith Minerals, and also gold projects. Activity is drilling and resource development funded by equity. Pre-revenue B2B junior with little consumer visibility. The discovery has drawn interest from major mining companies, and Rumble holds other Western Australian gold and lithium targets in addition.

Canadian mining company that appears to be a royalty or streaming vehicle focused on precious metals, located in Vancouver. Clinical-stage medical technology company developing the Selective Cytopheretic Device (SCD), a cartridge placed in a blood-filtration circuit that reduces inflammatory cells in acute kidney injury and sepsis. Its first product, Quelimmune, received US approval for use in children with acute kidney injury in 2024. Customers are hospitals and intensive-care units. Came public via a 2022 SPAC merger and trades on Nasdaq (ICU). Loss-making, limited revenue so far, little public brand awareness.

Silver-focused exploration company with polymetallic projects in North America, including the Red Mountain project in Alaska and the Adams Plateau project in British Columbia. Activities are drilling and resource definition, financed by equity placements. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. Pre-revenue and B2B, with no consumer brand profile. The company positions itself as a pure-play silver explorer for investors, with drilling campaigns funded through placements and no producing assets.

Exploration company developing the Thompson Brothers lithium project in Manitoba, Canada, a spodumene pegmatite deposit it aims to take into production for lithium-ion battery supply chains. Listed on Nasdaq (LITM) and the Canadian market. Pre-revenue, funded by equity raises, with delivery depending on permitting and financing. B2B developer with no consumer visibility. The project lies near the Snow Lake mining district, which has existing mining infrastructure, power and a skilled workforce, an advantage for development.

Medical device company that makes PediGuard and DSG (Dynamic Surgical Guidance) technologies, handheld devices that sense electrical conductivity to warn surgeons when a drill nears the edge of a vertebra during spinal screw placement. Sells through distributors and partners to spine surgeons and hospitals in the US, Europe and Asia; has partnered with Zimmer Biomet and others. Listed on Euronext Growth Paris (ALSGD). Niche B2B brand.

Critical-minerals explorer focused on platinum-group metals, nickel and copper in the Stillwater complex area of Montana, the only major US source of platinum and palladium. Holds the Stillwater West project and is drilling to define resources, with US supply-chain security as selling point. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (PGE). Pre-revenue, little consumer visibility. It markets itself as a domestic source of critical minerals, a theme that aligns with US policy interest in reducing reliance on imported platinum-group metals.

Medical device company making the XTRAC excimer laser and VTRAC lamp systems for treating psoriasis, vitiligo and eczema in dermatology clinics, plus TheraClear acne devices and Pharos lasers. Revenue comes from recurring treatment use and device placement with dermatologists, across the US. Listed on Nasdaq (SSKN). Known to dermatologists; patients know the treatment more than the brand. Strata's customers are dermatology practices that buy or lease devices, and the company earns recurring fees per treatment as well as one-time equipment sales.

Gold company with the Buckreef gold project in northwestern Tanzania, operated through a joint venture with the Tanzanian state-owned mining company STAMICO, plus earlier exploration holdings in the country. Sells gold produced at Buckreef to refiners. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and OTC (TNX). B2B miner with no brand visibility outside its sector. The project was scaled to a small-scale operation and is being expanded, and the company also has legacy exploration licences in the Lake Victoria goldfields region.

Canadian precious-metals exploration company based in British Columbia, listed in Canada. Specific projects, results and financing cannot be confirmed from the information available. Peruvian zinc and silver explorer, with the Ayawilca project in the central Andes of Peru, a large zinc-silver-indium-tin deposit with a resource estimate; also the Colquipucro silver project. Royalty company spun out of Vizsla Silver in 2024, owning royalty interests in mining projects in Mexico and elsewhere, giving it exposure to production revenue without operating mines. Income comes from royalty payments and the company grows by buying or originating new royalties. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. B2B resource finance, no consumer brand. Its pitch to investors is a diversified set of royalties on silver and gold projects, with revenue that carries lower operating cost risk than owning mines.

Texas community bank, subsidiary of Spirit of Texas Bancshares, with branches in the Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio and Austin areas offering commercial, real estate and consumer lending and deposits to small businesses and households; about $3bn in assets. Public on Nasdaq (STXB) until Simmons Bank bought it, completed in 2022. Regional retail brand. The bank focused on small and mid-sized business lending and had grown through acquisitions of other Texas community banks before the sale.

US gold and copper explorer: its flagship CK Gold project in Wyoming is a development-stage open-pit gold project, plus the Keystone and Challis Gold projects in Nevada and Idaho. Management is working on permitting and project financing; no gold production or revenue. Listed on Nasdaq (USAU). B2B explorer with no consumer visibility. The company is targeting a mine that would sell gold doré to refiners, and it also earned small income from land and royalty arrangements.

Brazilian diagnostic medicine group offering imaging (MRI, CT, ultrasound, X-ray) and clinical laboratory services through a network of clinics and hospital-based units, led by brands such as Alliar, Alta Excelencia and Diagnostico. Serves health insurers, hospitals and patients across Brazil. Was listed on the B3 exchange (AALR3). Regional healthcare brand known locally. The group grew by acquiring regional diagnostic operators, and it competes with larger Brazilian laboratory chains such as Fleury and Dasa.

Rare-earth explorer listed on the ASX (ARR) developing the Halleck Creek project in Wyoming, where it has defined a large rare-earth resource, and the Cowboy State Mine, plus lithium and other holdings. Aims to supply heavy and light rare-earth oxides for magnets for US supply chains. Pre-revenue, equity funded; B2B with little consumer brand. The company is focused on proving up the resource and securing US federal and offtake support, given rare earths' use in magnets, defence and electronics.

US mortgage real-estate investment trust that held residential agency mortgage-backed securities and invested in mortgage servicing rights, earning net interest income and paying dividends. Listed on the NYSE (AI) and managed internally from northern Virginia. Ellington Financial acquired it in 2023, so it no longer trades independently. Financial vehicle with no consumer profile. Its income depended on the spread between mortgage-securities yields and its financing costs, so interest rates drove results. Tax rules for REITs required it to distribute most earnings.

Gold company advancing the Bullfrog Gold project in Nevada's Beatty district, with Reward and other adjoining claims it acquired in a 2021 merger, and a plan to restart past-producing open pits. Part of the Augusta group of companies led by Richard Warke. Listed on the TSX (G). Pre-revenue, B2B, and without consumer awareness. The plan is a heap-leach gold operation using existing Nevada infrastructure, and the company is advancing permitting and feasibility work.

Early-stage medical technology company developing a catheter-based sensor system to detect and treat pain-causing nerve signals, aiming to apply it to cancer-related pain and other conditions with a potential non-opioid alternative. Pre-revenue and in clinical studies, funded by public offerings. Listed on Nasdaq (AMIX) after a 2023 IPO. Little public recognition. Its technology uses a nanoscale sensing array on a catheter tip, and early human data supports further trials, but it has no approved product yet.

Quebec lithium developer with the Rose lithium-tantalum project near Eastmain in the James Bay region, plus the Pivert deposit. Targets spodumene concentrate for battery makers. Air pollution control and chemical technology company. World-leading coloured gemstone miner, mining Zambia's Kagem emerald mine and the Montepuez ruby mine in Mozambique, with auctions of rough stones to jewellers and traders worldwide. South Carolina community bank, subsidiary of GrandSouth Bancorporation, with branches in Greenville, Columbia and the Upstate offering business loans, mortgages and deposits. About $1.2bn in assets. Precious-metals company with gold projects in Mexico, led by the Ana Paula gold project in Guerrero and the San Agustin project in Durango, aiming for production through development or restart. Michigan bank holding company for Isabella Bank, with about 30 branches across central and western Michigan serving farmers, small businesses and households with agricultural, commercial and consumer lending, deposits, wealth and insurance services. Newfoundland-focused gold developer with the Hammerdown gold project and the Green Bay property, a past-producing mine area it is advancing towards restart, backed by funding from Orion Mine Finance. Owner of specialty surgical hospitals and surgery centres in the United States, listed in Toronto (DR). Low public brand awareness. Profitability depends on surgical volumes at its hospitals and reimbursement rates, and the company paid regular dividends to shareholders.

Copper exploration company holding mining licences around Solwezi in Zambia's North-Western province, close to the large Kansanshi and Lumwana mines, working on exploring the Kitumba and nearby prospects. Pre-revenue, funded by equity raises. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (MMA). B2B explorer. The Zambian Copperbelt is a leading global copper region, which is why juniors have targeted licences near operating mines.

Silver explorer holding the Alamos silver project in Sonora, Mexico, a large epithermal silver district it is drilling to build resources. Previously known as Minaurum Gold and associated with the Mexican exploration community. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. Pre-revenue, equity funded, no consumer exposure. The district is known for historic silver-gold mining, and the company has been expanding drilling to define a potential bulk-tonnage target.

Maker and direct seller of herbal and nutritional supplements, essential oils, personal care and weight-management products under the Nature's Sunshine and Synergy brands, sold through independent distributors in a multi-level-marketing model in about 40 countries. Revenue around $450m a year. Founded in 1972 and listed on Nasdaq (NATR). Brand known mainly to supplement users and distributors. Its manufacturing is in Utah, and sales reach distributors in North America, Asia and Europe, with the business built on direct sales and recruitment.

Closed-end fund managed by OFS Capital Management that invests mainly in collateralised loan obligation (CLO) equity and junior debt tranches, aiming to pay regular distributions to shareholders. Listed on Nasdaq (OCCI), with shares sold to retail income investors. A financial vehicle with no operating business or consumer brand. The fund's income comes from CLO payments and its performance depends on credit conditions in the US leveraged loan market.

Gold exploration company advancing the Munro-Croesus project in the Abitibi greenstone belt near Timmins, Ontario, and other Canadian properties, funded through equity and focused on drilling. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. Pre-revenue B2B explorer. The Timmins and Abitibi region has produced more than 70 million ounces of gold, and Onyx targets drilling extensions of historic high-grade veins. It reports assay results from its drilling to the market regularly.

Mineral development company with the Mabilo copper-gold-iron project on Camarines Norte in the Philippines, which it moved into production and iron-ore export, plus other Asian exploration. Production at Mabilo has involved mining, processing copper-gold ores and exporting iron concentrate to customers, mainly in Asia, while the company seeks to expand.

Connecticut community bank, subsidiary of Salisbury Bancorp (Nasdaq: SAL), with branches in Connecticut, Massachusetts and New York offering commercial lending, mortgages, deposits and wealth advisory to local businesses and households. About $1.5bn in assets. NBT Bancorp acquired it in 2023. Local retail bank. Its operations include trust and wealth advisory, and the bank traces its roots to 1848, making it one of Connecticut's oldest banks.

South Korean video-game developer behind Stellar Blade, a PlayStation 5 action game launched in 2024, and Goddess of Victory: NIKKE, a mobile shooter-gacha game that earns most revenue in Asia and the West. Mineral exploration company listed on the ASX (SVM) developing Kasiya, one of the world's largest natural rutile and graphite deposits, in Malawi, intended to supply titanium dioxide pigment and welding markets as well as battery graphite. Rio Tinto is a major shareholder. Pre-revenue; B2B resource company with strong institutional backing but no consumer brand. The project's scale, near Malawi infrastructure and an environmentally lighter mining method, has attracted strategic investors and been tested in feasibility work.

Uranium explorer with prospective properties in Canada's Athabasca Basin, Saskatchewan, and other uranium-bearing areas, funded by equity raises. Listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange / TSX Venture. Pre-revenue, B2B, no consumer exposure. Uranium demand is linked to nuclear power, and the company's work consists of exploration drilling and geophysical surveys on its claims. The company has no revenue and relies on investors to fund its work programmes each year.

Maker of safety controls and electrical components for kettles and small appliances, plus water products. Brands and businesses include Strix thermostats and the Billi boiling and chilled water taps (Australia) and Aqua Optima water filters. Customers are appliance brands and the retail and commercial water markets. Based on the Isle of Man with manufacturing in the UK and China, listed on London's AIM (KETL). B2B supplier.

Swedish cleantech firm that makes Stirling engine-based systems converting industrial waste heat into electricity, also offering heat-and-power units; customers are industrial plants. Produces from its Gothenburg area base and raised funding for expansion. Listed on a Swedish growth market. B2B equipment supplier, little consumer recognition. The company's pitch is industrial energy efficiency, helping customers cut fuel costs and emissions by recovering waste heat from furnaces and engines.

US consumer health company behind FOCUSfactor, a brain-health supplement, Flat Tummy Tea, Hand MD and other lifestyle products, sold at Costco, Walmart, Amazon and online. Controlled by Jack Ross, formerly publicly quoted over the counter. Consumer brands with mass-market distribution in the US. The business relies on retail partnerships and online advertising, and has grown by acquiring brands from other consumer health companies.

UK regenerative medicine company that makes tissue products using its dCELL technology, which strips cells from donor tissue to leave a biocompatible scaffold. Products include SurgiPure, BioRinse, DermaPure and other acellular dermal matrices for wound care, orthopaedics and cardiology. Customers are surgeons and clinics in the US and UK. Listed on London's AIM (TRX). B2B healthcare brand. Its largest market is the US, and the group sold some legacy business lines to focus on its core regenerative medicine and wound care products.

Conversational AI company selling digital sales agents (branded as DISA) that make and take outbound calls and chats for businesses in sectors such as insurance, financial services and telecom. Based in the US and listed on Nasdaq (VHAI) after a 2024 IPO. Revenue is small and losses are large. B2B software with limited visibility. Its customers use the AI to cut call-centre labour costs, and it is an early-stage company that depends on adoption by a handful of clients.

Australian gas explorer with a stake in the West Erregulla gas field in the Perth Basin of Western Australia, a joint venture with Strike Energy. Hancock Energy, backed by Gina Rinehart's Hancock Prospecting, acquired Warrego in 2022. B2B energy company. The gas field is seen as a key supply source for Western Australia's domestic gas market, serving power and industrial customers.

Mining exploration company based in Tucson, Arizona, with interests in Alaska according to its name. Project names, results and financing cannot be confirmed from the information available. Consumer products business best known for Yowie, a chocolate confectionery with a collectible toy inside, sold in Australia, the US and elsewhere. Has pursued licensing and entertainment. Reached investors with a US listing; revenue is small. Candy for children, with some brand recognition among families. The brand originated in Australia as a cousin of Kinder surprise-style products, and its collectibles are often marketed to children via retailers.

UK-listed oil and gas company with operations in the Paradox Basin of Utah and in the Williston Basin of North Dakota, drilling and developing oil and gas assets. Listed on London's AIM (ZPHR). Revenue from oil sales is modest. B2B energy producer with a low profile. The company's strategy is to grow production in the US through drilling, and it has used horizontal wells in Utah's Paradox Basin.

US tobacco and nicotine group. Sells Marlboro, the best-selling US cigarette, through Philip Morris USA, plus Copenhagen and Skoal smokeless products through US Smokeless Tobacco, on! nicotine pouches and NJOY e-vapor (acquired 2023); holds a stake in beer giant AB InBev. Revenue about $20bn net, almost entirely from US adult smokers via convenience stores. Listed on the NYSE (MO). Marlboro is a global-scale brand name (international rights belong to Philip Morris International), though tobacco advertising is legally restricted.

Pharmaceutical services company, once the largest contract research organisation in the world, running clinical trials for drug makers and providing commercial consulting. Went public on the NYSE in 2013 after private equity ownership by TPG and Bain, then merged with IMS Health in 2016 to form QuintilesIMS, renamed IQVIA in 2017. The Quintiles name no longer exists as a separate company. B2B pharma services brand.

French agricultural cooperative group with roughly 10,000 farmer-members in the Champagne region and nearby, collecting and selling cereals, and processing them into malt, flour and bakery products. Businesses include Malteurop (one of the world's largest maltsters), Vivescia Industries and milling and bakery subsidiaries serving food producers and retailers. Revenue several billion euros. Formed in 2012 from Champagne Cereales and Nouricia. Mostly B2B, though some bakery and cereal products reach shoppers.

French sugar-beet cooperative group owned by around 9,000 growers, running sugar factories at Bazancourt, Erstein and elsewhere, and producing white sugar, alcohol and bioethanol, animal feed and renewable energy. Consumer brands include Daddy and Erstein sugar in French supermarkets. Revenue about EUR 2bn. Third-largest sugar group in Europe after Sudzucker and Tereos. Strong grocery name in France. The group sells to food manufacturers and retailers, and exports sugar across Europe and other regions, but its household names are mainly Daddy and Erstein.

Drug and device developer behind ITCA 650, a matchstick-sized osmotic mini-pump implanted under the skin to release exenatide continuously for a year in type 2 diabetes. Founded in 1995, valued at multibillion dollars by private funding, with Servier and Boehringer Ingelheim deals. The FDA rejected it repeatedly, and the company lost its backers, run into legal disputes with a lender, and wound down around 2021 with assets sold. No longer an active brand.

Chinese mRNA biotechnology company based in Suzhou, which developed a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine candidate together with Walvax Biotechnology and Academy of Military Medical Sciences. Platform covers lipid nanoparticle delivery and mRNA drug development for infectious disease and cancer. Backed by private investors and Walvax. B2B biotech with some public profile in China from the pandemic. Its mRNA programmes have included COVID-19 and other vaccines, and its Chinese vaccine peers faced strong competition after the pandemic.

Biotech developing protein therapeutics that target TGF-beta superfamily pathways. Its product luspatercept, sold as Reblozyl by Bristol Myers Squibb, treats anaemia in beta thalassaemia and myelodysplastic syndromes, and sotatercept targeted pulmonary arterial hypertension. Merck acquired Acceleron in November 2021 for roughly $11.5bn, and it no longer trades separately. Pharma B2B brand. The company was based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and its programmes reflected a strategy of building protein drugs for rare blood and lung diseases.

Chinese genomics company, a listed subsidiary of BGI Group, that designs and manufactures DNA sequencers on its DNBSEQ technology, sample preparation systems and lab automation, with a competing position to Illumina outside China. Customers are hospitals, research labs and testing firms globally. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market (688114). B2B instrument maker. The company has expanded overseas with offices in the US and Europe, positioning itself as a lower-cost alternative in the sequencing market.

Pharma company developing treatments for rare epilepsies, notably Fintepla (fenfluramine) for Dravet syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, plus Ztalmy for CDKL5 deficiency disorder. Listed on Nasdaq (ZGNX) and acquired by UCB in March 2022 for about $1.9bn, becoming part of a Belgian pharma group. Specialty pharma sold to neurologists. Zogenix had grown rapidly on Fintepla's rare-epilepsy launch, and the business was based in Emeryville, California.

Oncology drug developer focused on precision therapy for cancers driven by gene alterations. Lead candidate repotrectinib (Augtyro) treats ROS1-positive lung cancer and NTRK-positive solid tumours. Bristol Myers Squibb bought the company in 2022 for $4.1bn, ending its Nasdaq listing (TPTX). Specialty pharma sold to oncologists. Its drug competes with Pfizer's crizotinib and other ROS1 drugs, and the acquisition gave Bristol Myers Squibb a new precision oncology franchise.

Ophthalmology company that launched Rhopressa and Rocklatan, daily eye drops for glaucoma and ocular hypertension, in the US, with Europe launches of Rhokiinsa. Manufacturing was in Ireland. Listed on Nasdaq (AERI) before Alcon bought it in 2022 for about $770m plus contingent payments. Specialty pharma sold to eye specialists. The company pursued a US sales force and European expansion, though it had never reported sustained profit before the sale.

Drug developer known for Belviq (lorcaserin), a weight-loss pill withdrawn from the US market in 2020 after a cancer-risk finding, and for etrasimod, a drug for ulcerative colitis. Based in San Diego with a manufacturing site in Switzerland, it sold Belviq licensing rights. Pfizer completed the $6.7bn acquisition in March 2022, ending its Nasdaq listing (ARNA). Arena had long been a research-driven company with partnerships with Eisai, and the deal was one of Pfizer's larger biotech buys.

Sickle cell disease company that marketed Oxbryta (voxelotor), a daily pill that raises haemoglobin in sickle-cell patients, from 2019. Listed on Nasdaq (GBT) before Pfizer acquired it in 2022 for about $5.4bn. Pfizer pulled Oxbryta from global markets in 2024 over safety concerns. Specialty pharma. It was a leading sickle cell player alongside Novartis and Vertex, though the drug's withdrawal ended its commercial success.

Digital health company whose app and site compare prescription drug prices across pharmacies and give consumers coupons that lower the cash price, along with GoodRx Gold subscriptions, telehealth and pharma manufacturer solutions. Revenue about $750m a year, mainly from pharmacy benefit managers paying fees when coupons are redeemed. Listed on Nasdaq (GDRX) since 2020. Well-known US consumer health brand with heavy advertising.

Chinese social and live-video company, renamed Hello Group in 2021. Operates Momo, a location-based social and live-streaming app, and Tantan, a dating app, with revenue mostly from virtual gifting, paid membership and advertising, plus overseas apps. Over 100m monthly users at peak. Listed on Nasdaq (MOMO) since 2014. Strong mobile app brand in China. Monetisation relies on virtual gifts bought during live streams, which are shared with performers, and the company also invested in overseas social apps.

Biopharma company marketing Tymlos (abaloparatide), a daily injection for osteoporosis in postmenopausal women, and developing other bone treatments. Sold in the US to endocrinologists and primary-care doctors. Listed on Nasdaq (RDUS) before Gurnet Point Capital and Patient Square Capital acquired it in 2022 for about $890m. Specialty pharma. The company had royalty and licensing deals in Japan with Teijin, and it sold Tymlos through its own specialty sales force in the US.

Contract manufacturer making components and finished devices for the medical device industry, using laser micromachining, precision tubing, catheters and other minimally invasive device parts. Customers are global medtech firms. Private-equity backed and expanded by several acquisitions. B2B outsourcing partner with little public recognition. Typical products include catheter shafts, stents and implants made to tight tolerances, so customers are device companies that outsource complex manufacturing.

Proteomics company whose SomaScan platform uses aptamers to measure thousands of proteins in a blood sample for drug discovery, diagnostics and population health research. Customers are pharma, academic centres and biobanks. Listed on Nasdaq (SLGC) via a 2021 SPAC merger and acquired by Standard BioTools in a deal closed in early 2024. B2B life-science tools brand. Its technology measures about 7,000 proteins per sample, which makes it attractive for large cohort studies, and the company sold to the NIH and pharma.

Genomic diagnostics company selling tests that help doctors decide cancer treatment: Afirma for thyroid nodules, Decipher for prostate cancer, Percepta for lung cancer and Envisia for lung disease. Revenue about $450m, from labs billing insurers and Medicare, plus a biopharma data business. Listed on Nasdaq (VCYT). Known to clinicians rather than the public. The company also operates its own clinical laboratories and has partnered with pharma on diagnostics, and revenue growth is driven by volume.

Oncology company with Cosela (trilaciclib), given before chemotherapy to protect bone marrow in small-cell lung cancer, and other cancer candidates. Listed on Nasdaq (GTHX) until Pharmacosmos agreed to buy it in 2024 for about $405m. Specialty pharma sold to oncologists. The company also tested trilaciclib in other cancers, and the product is supplied to US hospitals and oncology clinics. Pharmacosmos is a privately held Danish drug company.

Family-controlled French holding company founded by the Merieux family that groups healthcare businesses: bioMerieux (in vitro diagnostics, listed in Paris), Transgene, Merieux NutriSciences (food testing), Merieux Equity Partners, and research and vaccine ties through the Fondation Merieux. Revenue and staff come largely from bioMerieux, with thousands of employees across the world. B2B, with little consumer brand profile. The group is a unique case of a family holding that reinvests in health research, with subsidiaries operating in dozens of countries.

Medical technology company whose SET pulse oximetry and patient-monitoring products are used in hospitals worldwide, along with the W1 health watch and Masimo Freedom consumer products. In 2022 it bought Sound United (Bowers & Wilkins, Denon, Marantz, Polk), and later agreed to sell the consumer audio business to Harman in 2025. Revenue about $2bn. Listed on Nasdaq (MASI). Strong clinician brand; consumer audio brands are well known.

Biopharma company led by founder Alan Auerbach, built around Nerlynx (neratinib), an oral drug for HER2-positive breast cancer, licensed from Pfizer, and other cancer candidates. Revenue about $200m a year, from US sales and partners in other regions. Listed on Nasdaq (PBYI). Specialty pharma, known to oncologists. The company has licensed Nerlynx rights to partners in Europe, China and other regions, and competes with Pfizer and Novartis in breast cancer.

Shenzhen-based Chinese company in hydrogen fuel-cell technology, and tagged for biotechnology and energy. Products, parent group and scale cannot be confirmed from the information available. The source entry offers no usable company description, so products, customers and size remain unverified. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Contract packaging and clinical-trial supply provider for pharmaceutical and biotech clients: primary and secondary packaging, labelling, cold-chain distribution and patient-supply services. Operates facilities in Pennsylvania, Tennessee and the UK. Previously part of Ireland's UDG Healthcare, it was later sold to private-equity investors. B2B service with low public profile. Its work includes labelling, kitting and shipping to investigator sites for clinical trials, so customers are drug developers rather than the public.

South Korean healthcare technology company developing artificial intelligence software that automates analysis of spinal images to support diagnosis. Customers, scale and ownership cannot be confirmed from the information available. The source entry offers no usable company description, so products, customers and size remain unverified. Biopharma company that developed izokibep, a small protein targeting IL-17A for psoriatic arthritis, hidradenitis suppurativa and uveitis, and lonigutamab for thyroid eye disease. Founded by Shao-Lee Lin and went public on Nasdaq (SLRN) in 2023 after a large private raise. Agreed to merge with Alumis in 2025. Drug developer with no consumer profile. The programme encountered regulatory setbacks, and the company cut staff before combining with Alumis in an all-stock deal.

Agricultural food-technology company with a crop-design platform producing high-protein, better-tasting soybeans and other ingredients, such as pea and soy proteins and oils, sold to food makers and animal feed customers. Went public through a SPAC (Star Peak II) on the NYSE (BHIL) in 2021, and filed for Chapter 11 in 2025 and sold off assets. Its customers were food and feed manufacturers, and the company had hoped to differentiate with high-protein soybeans, but it struggled with cash and losses.

Indoor vertical-farming company that grew leafy greens and herbs with robotics, vision systems and its BoweryOS software, sold under the Bowery brand through Whole Foods, Walmart, Amazon Fresh and other grocers. Raised over $700m at a valuation near $2bn but shut down in late 2024. Consumer food brand with some national retail distribution while operating. The company operated large farms in New Jersey, Maryland and Georgia and had backing from investors including GV and Temasek before closure.

Genomics company that built a low-cost DNA sequencer, the UG 100, aiming for a $100 genome and high throughput for research, single-cell and clinical genomics. Founded in 2016 by Gilad Almogy and emerged from stealth in 2022 with backing from Founders Fund, Khosla and others. Customers are large genomics labs and researchers. B2B instrument maker. It competes with Illumina, Element Biosciences and others, and has sold its machines to genomics service providers, population studies and clinical labs.

Vietnam's largest residential property developer, a subsidiary of conglomerate Vingroup, building large integrated townships such as Vinhomes Ocean Park, Vinhomes Grand Park and Vinhomes Smart City around Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Revenue comes from home and apartment sales to Vietnamese buyers plus leasing. Listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (VHM). Vingroup also owns VinFast and Vinpearl; strong domestic brand.

Biopharma company using an expanded genetic code to build precisely made antibody-drug conjugates and other protein medicines, with cancer drugs such as ARX788 for HER2 cancers. Originally founded by Peter Schultz, it had a Chinese arm and listed on Nasdaq (AMAM) in 2023. Johnson & Johnson acquired Ambrx in 2024 for about $2bn. Drug developer. The technology enables conjugation at defined sites, which should make drugs more consistent, and the company also had Chinese partnership deals.

mRNA medicines and vaccines company with LUNAR lipid-nanoparticle delivery and STARR self-amplifying RNA technology. Its COVID vaccine Kostaive (ARCT-154), partnered with CSL Seqirus, was approved in Japan in 2023 and in Europe in 2025, and it works on rare liver and lung diseases. Listed on Nasdaq (ARCT). B2B biotech. Revenue comes from collaboration and licensing payments rather than product sales, and the company is based in San Diego.

Biopharma company that developed Korsuva (difelikefalin), an injection for itch in dialysis patients with chronic kidney disease, sold in the US by Vifor and Fresenius. Listed on Nasdaq (CARA). Reverse merged with Tvardi Therapeutics in 2025. Drug developer with no consumer profile. The product's main sales were in dialysis clinics, and the company's earlier candidates in other pain indications did not succeed.

Privately held research-driven pharma group founded in 1950 and owned by the Paulsen family, with products in reproductive health (Menopur, Rekovelle), urology (Firmagon, Adstiladrin for bladder cancer), gastroenterology (Pentasa, Colazide) and maternal health. Sells in over 100 countries to hospitals and clinics, with several thousand employees and revenue more than $2bn. B2B, known mainly to clinicians. Ferring is headquartered in Switzerland, and among the best known of its products is Menopur, widely used in fertility clinics.

Genetic-medicine company with ceDNA technology, a non-viral way to deliver gene therapy to the liver and other tissues, targeting diseases such as hemophilia. Listed on Nasdaq (GBIO) and has had partnership deals with Moderna and Takeda. Pre-revenue, restructured in recent years. B2B biotech. The company has restructured and trimmed staff to extend its cash, and relies on collaborations to pay for development.

Oncology company whose Elahere (mirvetuximab soravtansine) antibody-drug conjugate treats folate-receptor-alpha-positive platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Based in Waltham, Massachusetts, listed on Nasdaq (IMGN). AbbVie acquired it in February 2024 for around $10bn. Specialty pharma. The drug was approved by the FDA in November 2022 and became a major product, and the transaction ended the Nasdaq listing. ImmunoGen was one of the longest-established antibody-drug conjugate companies, founded in 1981.

Genome-engineering company developing a benchtop CRISPR instrument, the Onyx, with its MAD7 gene-editing enzyme, selling to biotech and agricultural researchers. Based in Boulder, backed by venture capital. The company wound down operations around 2023. B2B life-science tools. It sold instruments and enzyme licences to researchers, but struggled against better-funded competitors in genome editing. Inscripta raised hundreds of millions of dollars from venture investors.

Gene-therapy company whose Vyjuvek (beremagene geperpavec) is a topical gel for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, approved by the FDA in May 2023 as the first redosable gene therapy, with Europe and Japan launches following. Revenue several hundred million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (KRYS). Specialty rare-disease company. Sales are driven by treating patients at home, and the company is also developing therapies for lung and eye diseases.

Japanese manufacturer in the semiconductor materials field, tagged for manufacturing and semiconductors, which works with silicon wafer processing. Biotech company working on oral integrin-targeting drugs for autoimmune diseases such as ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease and fibrosis, including candidate MORF-057. Listed on Nasdaq (MORF). Morphic grew from research by Timothy Springer at Harvard and had a partnership with AbbVie.

Gene therapy company that developed Strimvelis for ADA-SCID and Lenmeldy (OTL-200), a one-time gene therapy for metachromatic leukodystrophy. Listed on Nasdaq (ORTX) and acquired by Kyowa Kirin in January 2024. Rare disease specialist sold to hospital treatment centres. Taiwanese biopharma listed on the Taipei exchange, best known for Besremi (ropeginterferon alfa-2b), a treatment for polycythemia vera approved in the US in 2021 and Europe earlier, sold with US operations in Massachusetts and Japan partners. Also works on cancer and hepatitis. Specialty pharma. The company is based in Taipei with a US subsidiary, and it has pursued new indications for its interferon platform.

Biotech that developed Tzield (teplizumab), the first drug to delay onset of type 1 diabetes, approved by the FDA in 2022. Listed on Nasdaq (PRVB). Sanofi bought the company in 2023 for about $2.9bn. Specialty pharma. The deal gave Sanofi a first-in-class diabetes drug that delays disease onset, which was approved in November 2022. The company was founded in 2016 and licensed teplizumab from MacroGenics.

Italian-origin maker of cartonboard from recycled fibres, used for packaging of food, cosmetics, pharma and household goods, operating mills in Italy, Germany, France, Spain and the UK. Formerly listed on Borsa Italiana as Reno De Medici, one of Europe's leading producers of recycled cartonboard. B2B packaging supplier, not visible to consumers. The company's customers include packaging converters in consumer goods, and its mills are positioned near major European markets.

Clinical research and commercialisation company that runs drug trials for pharma and biotech clients and handles marketing and medical communications for launching drugs. Formed in 2017 from INC Research and inVentiv Health, with about 25,000 staff. Taken private by Elliott, Patient Square and Veritas in 2023 for about $7bn. B2B. It is headquartered in North Carolina's Research Triangle, serving the entire drug development cycle from trial design to commercial launch.

Synthetic-biology company that engineered probiotic bacteria as living medicines for rare metabolic diseases such as phenylketonuria and homocystinuria. Listed on Nasdaq (SYBX), partnered with Roche and Ginkgo, and shut down its programme in 2024 after a trial failure and ended its trading. B2B biotech. The company was a pioneer in engineered bacteria as medicines, and it shut down after its late-stage trial failed to show benefits.

Women's health pharma company selling Bijuva (estradiol and progesterone capsule for menopause symptoms), Imvexxy (vaginal inserts) and Annovera ring. Based in Florida, listed on Nasdaq (TXMD). Sold its commercial products to Mayne Pharma in 2022 and became a licensing and royalty entity. Specialty pharma. The company had a field sales force in the US to promote its products to obstetrician-gynaecologists, and it was heavily indebted.

Belgian maker of biological crop protection and pollination products: bumblebees, beneficial insects and mites, biocontrol agents, plus pollination services for greenhouse growers. Customers are fruit and vegetable growers worldwide, and it acquired Brazil's Biotrop in 2023. Listed on Euronext Brussels (BIOB), now named BioFirst. B2B ag supplier. The group has operations in more than 70 countries and is a leader in bumblebee pollination for tomato and berry crops.

Fixed-income asset manager serving institutions, formerly the asset management arm of bond insurer MBIA and managing bonds for insurance companies, public funds and corporations. Insight Investment, owned by BNY Mellon, acquired it in 2016. Institutional B2B brand with no public profile. It was headquartered in Armonk, New York, and managed assets in corporate, municipal and structured credit portfolios. It served mostly institutional clients.

Indian outsourcing and analytics firm offering data management, digital operations and analytics to financial services, retail and manufacturing clients, including investment banks and capital-markets firms. Roughly 18,000 employees across India, the US and Europe. Founded in 2000 and listed on India's BSE and NSE. B2B services brand. Its business moves between data operations, analytics and software engineering, and a significant share of staff is based in Mumbai.

Microbiome biotech developing orally delivered biologics using non-living bacterial agents for inflammatory diseases. Listed on Nasdaq (EVLO), it wound down in 2023 after failing to advance its programme. B2B biotech. The company pursued orally delivered, non-living microbial products, and it was based in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Evelo was founded by Flagship Pioneering and went public in 2018; its candidates were tested for conditions such as atopic dermatitis and COVID-19.

Swiss contract manufacturer for pharma and life sciences. Makes drug substances and drug products, including biologics, cell and gene therapies, capsules and health ingredients, and serves most big pharma firms with plants in Visp (Switzerland), Portsmouth (US) and Asia. Revenue about CHF 6.7bn. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (LONN). B2B, with a high reputation in pharma. The company has a long history in Valais, Switzerland, and its largest division is biologics and cell therapy manufacturing.

Cell and gene therapy developer using piggyBac and Cas-CLOVER gene-engineering for CAR-T therapies against blood cancers and solid tumours. Listed on Nasdaq (PSTX), and Roche bought it in January 2025 for about $1.5bn. B2B biotech. The deal gave Roche a gene-engineering platform and a pipeline of allogeneic CAR-T therapies, with programmes in multiple myeloma and lupus. The company was founded in 2014 by Eric Ostertag.

Food maker producing plant-based beverages such as oat, almond and soy milks and fruit-based snacks, mostly as private-label and co-manufacturing for big retailers and brands, with plants across North America. Revenue about $700m. Listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (STKL). Consumer-facing products but brand is mainly retailers'. The company converted its portfolio to a focused plant-based beverage and food model, and shifted from natural ingredients toward packaged consumer products.

Biotech developing verekitug, an antibody targeting the TSLP receptor for severe asthma and other respiratory diseases. Listed on Nasdaq (UPB) via a 2024 IPO. Pre-revenue drug developer. The company's lead drug is being tested in adults with asthma, with later studies planned in other respiratory conditions. The company launched in 2021 with backing from Atlas Venture, and the drug is also being developed for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps.

Gene-editing company developing one-time base-editing treatments to lower cholesterol by switching off PCSK9 in the liver, including VERVE-102, aimed at heart disease. Listed on Nasdaq (VERV) and Eli Lilly agreed to acquire it in 2025. Pre-revenue drug developer. Verve's lead products were first-in-human, and the company licensed some technologies from Beam Therapeutics. Verve was founded in 2018 by Sekar Kathiresan, Kiran Musunuru and David Liu.

Korean food-delivery giant that runs Baedal Minjok (Baemin), the leading food-delivery app in South Korea, plus B Mart quick-commerce and restaurant ordering services. Revenue comes from commissions, advertising and delivery fees. Delivery Hero acquired it in 2019 for about $4bn. Strong consumer brand in Korea. Woowa Bros also made the Baemin delivery brand known through a quirky advertising style and fan events in Korea.

Swiss-French biotech developing antibodies against claudin-1, a protein involved in liver fibrosis, liver cancer and other diseases, with lead candidate ALE.F02 for fibrosis. The company's science uses Cl-1 antibodies in chronic liver disease, and its backers include European life-science investors. The firm has been growing its team in Switzerland and France.

San Francisco biotech developing antibody treatments for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, including a candidate targeting PSGL-1 (neihulizumab) for inflammatory bowel disease and graft-versus-host disease. Biotech formerly known as Progenity, which pivoted from diagnostic testing to oral biotherapeutics delivered through a smart pill for inflammatory bowel disease. Listed on Nasdaq (BIOR). Biotech developing in vivo CAR-T therapies using lipid nanoparticles to deliver mRNA that reprogramme immune cells inside the body, aimed at autoimmune disease and cancer. Canadian specialty pharma company that sells branded cardiovascular and mental-health drugs, notably Vascepa in Canada and Clozaril in the US, through licensing and acquisitions. Genomics and health-intelligence company founded by J. Craig Venter that offers whole-genome sequencing, full-body MRI and lab tests through its Health Nucleus clinic, plus data for pharma partners. Immuno-oncology biotech with offices in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Gosselies, Belgium, developing antibodies including belrestotug, a TIGIT inhibitor partnered with GSK. Listed on Nasdaq (ITOS). Clinical-stage biotech developing treatments for blood disorders and cardiopulmonary disease based on the TGF-beta pathway, including elritercept for myelodysplastic syndromes (licensed in part to Takeda) and KER-012. Listed on Nasdaq (KROS). B2B drug developer. Its drugs act on bone morphogenetic and activin pathways, and the company is funded through public offerings and partnerships. Keros was founded in 2015 and went public in 2020.

Icelandic land-based salmon farming project on the Westman Islands, planning large recirculating aquaculture capacity for Atlantic salmon. Aims to supply European and US seafood markets with sustainably farmed fish. Venture and infrastructure financed. Pre-revenue, B2B. The company plans to produce tens of thousands of tonnes of salmon, using geothermal and renewable energy in Iceland. Chinese ophthalmology pharma company that licenses and develops eye drugs and devices for diseases like dry eye, uveitis and retinal conditions in China and Asia. Listed in Hong Kong (1477). Medical-device company focused on children's orthopaedics, selling implants and instruments for scoliosis, trauma and sports injuries to paediatric surgeons and hospitals in the US and international markets. It also supplies products for paediatric fracture and deformity care, and has been selling through distributors across more than 50 countries.

Specialty pharma that markets Exparel, a long-acting local anaesthetic given at surgery to reduce opioid use, plus Zilretta and iovera for pain. Revenue around $700m, from hospitals and surgery centres. Listed on Nasdaq (PCRX). B2B, known to anaesthesiologists. The company also has manufacturing in California, and its flagship drug is used in millions of surgeries each year. It started as part of SkyePharma and went public in 2011.

Cell-therapy company developing REACT, an autologous kidney cell treatment for chronic kidney disease, via a 2022 SPAC merger. Listed on Nasdaq (PROK). Pre-revenue drug developer. The company is developing a cell therapy aimed at slowing kidney disease progression, and it has late-stage trials. ProKidney is running late-stage studies of its autologous treatment for patients with diabetes and chronic kidney disease, and is backed by Social Capital Hedosophia.

Biotech using antisense oligonucleotides to raise protein levels in genetic diseases; lead candidate zorevunersen for Dravet syndrome is in late-stage trials with Biogen as partner. Listed on Nasdaq (STOK). Pre-revenue drug developer. The medicine aims to increase production of a protein from the healthy copy of a gene, and the company is based in Massachusetts. It was founded in 2014 and went public in 2019.

Singapore- and UK-based biotech developing HMTM (hydromethylthionine), a drug that targets tau protein for Alzheimer's disease and behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia. Founded by scientist Claude Wischik and privately financed. B2B drug developer. The company is run from Aberdeen in Scotland and Singapore, and has sought regulatory approval in the UK and elsewhere. Its drug, called LMTM in earlier trials, has been tested in thousands of patients over more than a decade.

Biotech developing pacibekitug, an antibody against interleukin-6 for cardiovascular inflammation. Listed on Nasdaq (TRML) and acquired by Novartis in 2025 for about $1.4bn. Drug developer. The drug is aimed at patients at risk of heart attack and stroke from persistent inflammation, and the buyout ended its Nasdaq listing. The drug is injected under the skin and was studied in people with elevated inflammation markers after heart attacks.

Swedish maker of products for assisted reproduction (IVF): culture media, incubators, cell-handling devices and genetic tests used in fertility clinics worldwide. Revenue about SEK 3.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (VITR). B2B med-tech brand. The group has subsidiaries across Europe, the US and Asia, and its customers are fertility clinics and embryologists. Vitrolife was founded in 1994 and holds leading positions in its markets.

Gene-therapy company applying AAV capsid engineering via its TRACER platform to deliver treatments to the central nervous system, partnered with Novartis, Neurocrine and others. Listed on Nasdaq (VYGR). B2B drug developer. Voyager has partnerships worth hundreds of millions of dollars in potential milestones and has focused on neurological diseases. Voyager was founded in 2013 in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The company is funded by partner payments and equity raises.

Belgian biotech based in Antwerp working on therapies for inflammatory and fibrotic diseases. Its pipeline and financing cannot be confirmed in detail.
