Healthcare subsidiary of Apollo Hospitals Enterprise, running Apollo Pharmacy, India's biggest pharmacy chain with roughly 6,000 stores, plus the Apollo 24/7 digital health platform and diagnostics. Revenue from medicine retail, online consultations and distribution. Strong consumer brand across India. Apollo HealthCo is listed after a demerger from its parent, and owns Apollo Pharmacy stores that dispense medicines to millions of customers.

Programmatic advertising platform that let advertisers and publishers buy and sell digital ads on its software. AT&T acquired it in 2018 for about $1.6bn and merged it into Xandr, which Microsoft bought in 2021. The AppNexus brand has been retired. B2B ad-tech. The company was based in New York and served advertising agencies and publishers who bought programmatic ads in real-time auctions.

Contract developer and manufacturer of biologics for biotech and pharma clients from facilities in California, offering cell-line development to commercial drug substance production. Listed on Nasdaq (CDMO) and acquired by GHO Capital and Ampersand Capital in 2025. B2B. Avid Bioservices makes products at its Tustin facility and has served customers in the US, Europe and Asia. The business was formerly Peregrine Pharmaceuticals before changing its name in 2018.

Cell-therapy company that developed firi-cel (firicabtagene autoleucel), a CD19 CAR-T, in lymphoma. Listed on Nasdaq (CRGX) and wound down in 2025 after weak results. Drug developer. CARGO ended development of its lead programme and decided to wind down, ending a short listing. CARGO was founded in 2019, raised a large IPO in November 2023, and tested its CAR-T in large B-cell lymphoma patients.

Performance-marketing and lead-generation firm connecting consumers searching online with service providers, in areas like home services, insurance and telecom, and running search and affiliate marketing. B2B agency known inside the ad industry. The firm is owned by private investors and generated revenue from clicks and leads sold to enterprise clients. Centerfield owns consumer-facing comparison websites and operates call centres. Revenue depends on advertiser demand and campaign volumes.

Interventional oncology company marketing the Hepzato Kit, a drug-device combination for liver-directed melphalan treatment of metastatic uveal melanoma, approved by the FDA in August 2023. Listed on Nasdaq (DCTH). Specialty medical device and drug company. The company's product is delivered at specialised cancer centres, and it began generating meaningful sales after launch. Delcath delivers melphalan in isolation to the liver, and the firm has a history of financial difficulty.

San Diego biotech developing treatments for respiratory and fibrotic diseases such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, based on taladegib. Venture-backed and private. Drug developer. The company is aimed at fibrotic lung disease, and its backers include investment funds and a founding team of drug developers. The company licensed taladegib from Eli Lilly and has been testing it in patients with the lung disease.

Biotech developing Endosomal Escape Vehicle (EEV) therapeutics for neuromuscular and other intracellular diseases, including Duchenne muscular dystrophy, partnered with Vertex. Listed on Nasdaq (TRDA). Drug developer. The company's science builds on cell-penetrating peptides, and it is conducting clinical trials in muscle diseases. Entrada was founded in 2016, listed on Nasdaq in 2021, and signed a Vertex partnership worth $224m upfront for Duchenne treatments.

Ghana's state cocoa regulator and trader, COCOBOD, which buys beans from farmers, sets farm-gate prices, and sells to chocolate makers and traders, accounting for a key share of the country's exports. Ghana is the world's second-largest cocoa producer. State-owned, B2B and very prominent in the cocoa trade. It supervises quality control, export sales and farmer services, and supplies a large share of global cocoa to chocolate makers such as Mondelez and Nestle.

California cannabis grower and brand house, the owner of Glass House Farms, producing from large greenhouses in Carpinteria and Camarillo, selling flower, pre-rolls and extracts, and operating retail stores. Revenue about $200m. Listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (GLAS.A). Consumer cannabis brand, with advertising limits. The company grows cannabis in sun-grown greenhouses, and also sells through its own dispensaries under the Farmer and the Felon name.

Biotech company working on rare-disease therapies, based in Palo Alto. Its programmes and funding cannot be confirmed from the information available. Nigerian digital payments company, owner of Verve card scheme, Quickteller consumer payments and a switching network for banks, merchants and governments across Africa. It processes billions of transactions a year and runs payment services for schools, governments and utility companies across Africa. Interswitch was founded in 2002.

Longevity-focused biotech company, founded by investor Jim Mellon, that builds and finances a portfolio of ageing-related drug programmes. Private. Drug developer with low public visibility. It has raised well over $100m from private investors and assembled a group of drug-development companies and programmes in ageing biology. It does not yet generate product revenue.

Taiwanese-run aquaculture technology firm that provides recirculating aquaculture systems and fish-farming consulting in Asia and Africa. Listed on Nasdaq (NCRA) after a 2022 IPO. B2B ag-tech. Nocera sells small recirculating fish-farming systems and consulting services, and it is a small company with revenue in the low millions. It also sells fish-farming equipment in Taiwan and has expanded into the US.

Swiss biotech spun out of Roche, developing drugs for neuropsychiatric disorders, with basimglurant for trigeminal neuralgia as lead candidate. Venture-backed. Drug developer. The company has an approach to neuropsychiatric disease, and it raised funding from investors including Roche Venture Fund. The company also develops treatments for Tourette syndrome and other psychiatric conditions using compounds licensed from Roche, and has raised over $100m.

Subsidiary of French nuclear group Orano, developing alpha-emitting lead-212 radiopharmaceuticals for cancer, with production facilities in the US and France. B2B drug developer. It plans to scale lead-212 supply, and it is working with cancer drug developers on targeted alpha therapy. Its lead candidate is AlphaMedix (212Pb-DOTAMTATE) for neuroendocrine tumours, supported by a dedicated production network in Europe and America.

Cancer genomics company providing NeXT Personal, a tumour-informed blood test for monitoring cancer recurrence, and sequencing services for pharma. Partners with Tempus and Moderna. Listed on Nasdaq (PSNL). B2B diagnostics. The company serves pharma customers who use its sequencing for clinical trials, and its test is covered by Medicare for some patients. Personalis was spun out of Stanford research in 2011.

Digital promotions and coupon company behind Coupons.com, which delivered manufacturer coupons to shoppers and retailers online. Listed on the NYSE (QUOT) and acquired by Neptune Retail Solutions in 2023. B2B ad-tech with consumer coupon brand. The company also sold digital advertising to consumer brands and retailers, and was based in Jersey City, New Jersey. The business was formerly known as Coupons.com Inc.

Biotech developing small-molecule CFTR modulators for cystic fibrosis aimed at doing better than existing Vertex drugs. Listed on Nasdaq (SION) via a 2025 IPO. Pre-revenue drug developer. Cystic fibrosis is a rare disease with a limited market, so competition from Vertex's established drugs is a key challenge. Sionna was founded in 2019 and targets the NBD1 domain of the CFTR protein, a new approach.

Diagnostics firm with the T2 Magnetic Resonance technology, which detects sepsis-causing bacteria and fungi in blood without waiting for culture. Listed on Nasdaq (TTOO). Financial difficulties led to delisting. B2B hospital diagnostics. Its tests are used in hospitals to identify infections faster, though the company suffered from limited sales and financial stress. T2 was founded in 2006 and listed in 2014.

Indian industrial group with businesses in chemicals (Chemplast Sanmar, PVC), engineering (cast products, valves), and shipping, plus operations in Egypt and Mexico. Founded in 1962. B2B conglomerate, largely unknown to consumers. The group is led by the Sanmar family, and has plants and offices in India, the US and other regions. Chemplast Sanmar is listed on Indian exchanges and is among India's larger PVC suppliers.

Canada's national laboratory for particle and nuclear physics, run by a consortium of universities, with a 520 MeV cyclotron. It produces medical isotopes, performs research and develops radiopharmaceutical production. Non-profit research institute, no commercial consumer brand. Mobile measurement and analytics platform that helps app marketers track installs, attribution and fraud. AppLovin acquired it in 2021 for about $1bn. B2B ad-tech for app developers. German biotech developing visugromab, an antibody against GDF-15 for cancer immunotherapy resistance, partnered with Nestle's venture arm. Private, venture-backed drug developer. Specialty pharma selling Firdapse for Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, Fycompa for epilepsy (acquired from Eisai) and Agamree for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Revenue about $500m. IT service management and customer service software provider whose Cherwell Service Management helps IT teams run service desks and workflows. Ivanti acquired it in 2021. B2B software. Web monetisation startup built on the Interledger protocol, letting users pay publishers via a subscription while browsing. Founded by Stefan Thomas and linked to the Ripple ecosystem. Bioscience firm making Organ-Chips, microfluidic devices lined with human cells that mimic organs, for drug-safety and toxicity testing. Customers are pharma and regulators; Emulate's Liver-Chip was accepted in an FDA programme. Private. B2B life-science tools. The organ models are used to test whether drug candidates are toxic to liver, kidney, lung and other tissues. The company was founded in 2013 as a spin-out from Harvard's Wyss Institute.

Pakistan's biggest urea fertiliser producer by output, selling Engro Zarkhez and other branded fertilisers to farmers via a dealer network, part of Engro Corporation. Capacity above two million tonnes of urea per year. Listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (EFERT). B2B brand with strong farmer recognition. The company sells to farmers across Pakistan's Punjab and Sindh provinces, and it is part of the Engro conglomerate led by the Dawood family.

Biopharma applying chemoproteomics to find small-molecule drugs against hard targets, with lead FMC-376 against KRAS G12C. Venture-backed, with a Boehringer Ingelheim partnership. Drug developer. Its approach uses chemical probes inside live cells, and the company is based near San Francisco. Frontier Medicines was founded in 2017 and signed a collaboration with AbbVie in 2021. The firm remains private and pre-revenue, funded by venture investors.
